Four project types · Four perspectives · Git for scholarly editing

Workshop

We develop our Git strategy together.

Plan a workshop for your scholarly edition—with suitable questions, participants and resources.

Plan your workshop ↓

Why a joint workshop?

Using Git also means deciding how editorial work is organised, checked and preserved. These decisions affect the whole project. We therefore recommend a joint workshop for every editorial team considering Git or already committed to using it. Starting with Git without developing a strategy is not a good foundation.

IT specialists can explain technical possibilities and implement solutions. The editorial team must take responsibility for scholarly and organisational decisions. A single Git expert should not carry that responsibility alone either. Everyone should understand the basic workflow and its consequences and contribute to the agreements. They do not all need to master the same technical tasks.

What we can gain

The workshop is also an opportunity to discover possibilities and improve established methods: what supports our research? How do we check changes? How do we want to collaborate? A practical introduction using your own texts often helps more than an abstract technical demonstration.

The outcome is an initial jointly agreed Git strategy, explicit open questions, responsible roles and next practical checks. Scholarly responsibility is shared; technical tasks can be distributed. The workshop is tailored to your project.
